channel.title: LaunchVault blog
channel.description: One founder breakdown a week, plus short guides on reading the numbers. Every number wears a label and a dated source.

item.title: Windmill Growth started with a $500-a-month LinkedIn service and now brings in about $118K a month
item.description: It began by selling likes and comments on founders' LinkedIn posts, then sold the bigger job: writing the posts.

item.title: Upscale B2B sold $3 email inboxes to cold-email agencies, then became one, and now makes about $99K a month
item.description: It started by selling the 'picks and shovels' of cold email (the tools everyone doing it needs): ready-to-send inboxes for a few dollars a month.

item.title: Stencil AI went from $16K to $63K a month in 2026 by fixing one boring job for tattoo artists
item.description: Two brothers, one of them a tattoo artist, built a tool that skips hours of hand-tracing. They charged from day one, sold on the web first, then put it…

item.title: Rezi started as a resume template on Reddit and made $216K in October 2026
item.description: A free template, four slow years, then an early bet on AI writing. October 2026 brought in $216,471, read straight from Stripe.

item.title: Mindset reached $24K a month by building on its team's YouTube audience first
item.description: The people behind some of YouTube's biggest motivation channels built an app for the same audience.

item.title: Gojiberry's waitlist of 2,000 paid nothing. A rebuild took it to $407K in one month
item.description: The first product got a big waitlist and zero sales. The team rebuilt it in weeks, then pushed it through Reddit and a dozen other channels at once.

item.title: DM Champ sat near $10K a month for a year, then hit $28K after it changed who it sells to
item.description: It started by waking up one clinic's old leads on WhatsApp, found customers through cold email, AppSumo (a site that sells lifetime deals on software)…

item.title: Boothie made $208K in five months by riding the digicam selfie trend on TikTok
item.description: A two-person team launched an AI selfie app in June 2026, aimed it at people already posting on TikTok, and passed $56K in a single month by October.

item.title: AEO Engine turned an old Amazon ad agency into a $204K month by renaming itself for the AI search wave
item.description: It did not start from zero. An Amazon marketing agency from 2018 re-launched as an 'answer engine' agency in January 2026, just as brands started asking…

item.title: What 'Verified' means on LaunchVault
item.description: Where our revenue numbers come from, why some are labelled Claimed, and why every number has a date.

item.title: Three ways to start small
item.description: A family member's problem, a service you can sell now, or a free version people can try. A real example of each.

item.title: Postiz: almost two years under $15K a month, then $431K
item.description: A social media scheduler built by one main developer. What he did, what the numbers did after each move, and what you can take from it.

item.title: How to read a revenue chart
item.description: MRR, all-time revenue, and what a sudden jump on the line actually means.
